description: List data sources, tools, and usage hints for this SURIMI model-output MCP server.
name: describe_model_capabilities

description:
Check CF-conventions compliance with a heuristic: a Conventions attribute that starts with CF, and latitude and longitude coordinates. A data variable without units gives a warning only.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_check_cf_compliance

description:
Compare two time-index ranges per region.

period_a and period_b are (start_step, end_step_inclusive) indices.
op is 'diff' (B - A) or 'ratio' (B / A).
`select` picks one coordinate value on an extra non-time, non-spatial axis;
an unselected one is reported in `unselected_dims`.
`region` restricts the comparison to one region name; omitted, every region
in the mask is compared.
name: model_compare_periods

description:
Structure of an EwE (Ecopath with Ecosim) model export (.eiixml):
model name, EwE/DB version, the full table inventory (name + declared
row/column count for every table in the file), and the functional-group
NAMES from the EcopathGroup table. Metadata and group names ONLY - never
the diet-composition matrix or Ecosim scenario tables, which this tool
does not read at all.

Call with no argument first to see which models exist (`models`, live
from object storage - never a hardcoded list, so a newly-uploaded model
appears without a server update). Call again with a `name` (matches
either the model's internal name or its filename, case-insensitively)
for the full table inventory of one model.

`functional_groups.declared_row_count` is the EcopathGroup table's Num
attribute as the file states it; `functional_groups.names_found`/`names`
are what this tool actually read from the file's `<Row>` elements. These
two numbers can differ - see `functional_groups.note` when they do, and
report `names_found`, not `declared_row_count`, as how many functional
groups are actually nameable here.

This is SURIMI ensemble model CONFIGURATION, not a simulation result -
running or solving the model is out of scope for this tool.
name: model_describe_ecosystem_model

description:
Return the full structure of a netcdf file: dimensions, variables, global attributes and the file's sha256.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_describe_file

description:
Describe one simulation run: its artifacts plus parsed metadata.

Returns {model, simulation_id, n_artifacts, last_modified, metadata,
artifacts:[{name, size, kind, access}], stale, note, partial,
partial_note} - or {error, stale, note, partial, partial_note} if no
matching run is found. `access` is 'inline' for text you can fetch with
model_get_artifact, or 'link' for any other file, which
model_get_artifact returns as a download link.
`metadata` is model-specific: for CMSY it names the STOCK the run
assessed - read it and report it, because the stock decides what the
run is about. stale=true means object storage was unreachable and
n_artifacts, last_modified, and every artifact `size` come from the
last good listing, not a fresh one - say so rather than presenting them
as current. partial=true means some objects were dropped from even a
fresh listing, so this run's artifact count/manifest may be short - say
that too. An "error: no simulation with id ..." while stale or partial
is true is NOT proof the run does not exist - it may simply be missing
from a degraded or short listing; say that rather than asserting the
run does not exist.
name: model_describe_simulation

description:
What a CMSY++ id_file.csv input or result-table column means and
what it decides - the vocabulary model_get_stock_status/
model_get_stock_trajectory assume the caller already has.

Covers, at minimum, 'btype', 'force.cmsy' and 'Resilience' (the three
id_file.csv fields that change which estimator runs or how), plus the
year-encoded result columns ('c50', 'F.Fmsy00', 'B30', ...: decodes the
two-digit year the same way model_get_stock_trajectory does, including
the century wrap at 50) and a handful of named result-table columns
('N bt', 'last.B_Bmsy', 'last.F_Fmsy'). Definitions are sourced from
GSA06_CMSY++_input files/README.txt and AA_CMSY++.R's own validation -
not invented - and each entry cites where.

Field names are matched case-insensitively with spaces/underscores
treated as '.', so 'btype', 'BType' and 'b_type' all resolve the same
entry. An unmatched field returns {error, known_fields} naming every
field this tool DOES know, rather than a silent guess.
name: model_explain_assessment_field

description:
Fetch one artifact from a run.

Text (csv, R, yaml, tex, ...) comes back inline as {kind:'text', name,
content, truncated, stale, note, partial, partial_note} - plus
`truncation_note` when truncated=true. Any other file (pdf, jpg, nc) comes
back as {kind:'link', name, url, stale, note, partial, partial_note}. The
`url` points to this server's /artifact route, which serves the file from
the server's local cache, so it is a download link to give the user and
NOT something to describe the contents of. The `url` is absolute when the
deployment sets SURIMI_PUBLIC_BASE_URL and relative to this server
otherwise. Never claim to have read a PDF. stale=true means the run
was looked up in a degraded (last-good) listing because object storage
was unreachable when it was scanned - the artifact itself is still
read from the server, but say the listing that found it may be outdated
rather than presenting it as current. partial=true means some objects
were dropped from even a fresh listing, so a "not an artifact of this
run" error may reflect a short manifest rather than the file truly being
absent - say so instead of asserting it does not exist. truncated=true
means `content` is a PREFIX of the file, cut at a fixed byte cap,
possibly mid-field or mid-row: never count, total, or summarise it as if
it were the whole file - a 46,436-row CSV can come back showing ~3,761
rows, and counting those and reporting "3,761 rows" states a number that
is wrong, not merely incomplete. Only quote from what is shown, and say
the file was truncated.
name: model_get_artifact

description:
The case-study contract: what SURIMI can model, over what area,
period, in what units, coded how. Parses
controller/northwestern_med/northwestern_med_contract.yaml: case study name,
start/end date, time step, CRS + grid (resolution, dimensions, bbox),
the standards block (which code standard each field uses - species,
gear, life stage, market, currency, country, measurement system/units),
market codes, currency codes, and counts of the species/fleet-segment
entries the contract lists. `fleet_segments` carries each segment's own
`model` assignment ("EwE" or "POSEIDON") - a per-fleet LABEL only: the
controller calls both services unconditionally for every fleet every
step, so this field says which model a fleet is ASSIGNED to for
after-the-fact splitting, not a switch that turns either model off.

`divergence_note` is present on every response and must not be dropped
when relaying this: it says that this is the northwestern_med contract,
that the bucket holds others (aegean_sea, anchovy_bay) which this tool
does not read, and that the older western_med copy no longer exists.

This is model configuration, not a simulation result.
name: model_get_contract

description:
Per-variable NaN counts and fraction. A very large variable is estimated from sampled steps and carries `sampled` true, with no exact count.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_get_coverage_summary

description:
Return lat/lon extents and grid sizes.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_get_spatial_bounds

description:
Current Kobe status (B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy, reference points) from a CMSY++
result table.

`phase` has NO default - it must be 'historical' (assessed from real
catch/abundance data) or 'simulation' (assessed from ecosystem-model-
simulated data, SURIMI-CMSY/server/StockAssessment.py's second run). A
run that carries no CMSY_output_historical.csv/CMSY_output.csv split at
all, only one unlabelled Out_..._id_file.csv result table, is refused for
EITHER phase rather than guessed. The error names that file so the
caller can fetch it directly with model_get_artifact instead of trusting
a label this tool invented.

Returns {stock, phase, source_file, btype, n_abundance_years, estimator,
estimator_note, biomass_ratio_to_bmsy, fishing_pressure_ratio_to_fmsy,
reference_points: {Bmsy, Fmsy, MSY}, stale, note, partial, partial_note}
on success, or {error, stale, note, partial, partial_note} otherwise.

Every point estimate (biomass_ratio_to_bmsy, fishing_pressure_ratio_to_fmsy,
and each reference point) comes back as {point, lcl, ucl, bound_meaning} -
NEVER the point alone. `bound_meaning` says outright that lcl/ucl are the
2.5th/97.5th percentile of the MCMC posterior, not a confidence interval
at any stated level - the CMSY++ column names ("lcl"/"ucl") suggest a
confidence limit, but AA_CMSY++.R never states one, so report the bound
that way rather than repeating the column's own naming.

`estimator` names which of AA_CMSY++.R's two fits (CMSY, catch only, or
BSM, catch + abundance index) the reported numbers came from, decided by
the SAME rule model_explain_assessment_field('btype') documents: BSM
only when btype != 'None' AND at least 5 usable abundance-index years
exist in the assessment window, CMSY otherwise regardless of the btype
label. `estimator_note` explains the specific reason for this run, and
says outright that a run's id_file.csv force.cmsy=TRUE would override
this even when BSM's own gate is met - a fact this tool cannot verify
because force.cmsy is an id_file.csv INPUT column, never written into
the 349-column result row this tool reads.
name: model_get_stock_status

description:
Year-indexed catch/F.Fmsy/B series from a CMSY++ result table.

Same `simulation_id`/`stock`/`phase` contract, lookup and refusal
behaviour as model_get_stock_status (see its docstring) - `phase` has no
default and a run with no historical/simulated split is refused by name
rather than guessed.

Returns {stock, phase, source_file, trajectory: [{year, catch, f_fmsy,
b}, ...], stale, note, partial, partial_note}. `trajectory` is sorted by
the DECODED year, oldest first - AA_CMSY++.R names its year columns
c50..c99 (1950-1999) then c00..c30 (2000-2030) in the SAME row, so
sorting the column names themselves would put 2000 before 1950. Years
where catch, F/Fmsy and B are all NA (the schema reaches to 2030
unconditionally, but a stock assessed only through, say, 2012 leaves
every later column empty) are dropped rather than returned as a row of
nulls - do not report "data through 2030" from this response's shape.
name: model_get_stock_trajectory

description:
Return start/end of the time axis as raw values with their units, and decoded to calendar dates (`start_iso`, `end_iso`, `start_year`, `end_year`) when the axis has usable CF units.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_get_time_range

description:
List the netcdf catalog so you can find a file from a plain question.

Returns {prefix, count, files:[{uri, size, kind}]} where kind is
'data', 'mask', or 'other', plus `notes` when a source could not be
listed and `stale` and `as_of` when a saved listing was served. Call this FIRST when asked about ocean/
biomass/gridded data, then model_describe_file on a chosen 'data' file to
see its variables, then an analytical tool (e.g. model_top_regions) with a
matching 'mask' file. Defaults to the SURIMI netcdf bucket prefix.

A file a SURIMI run wrote also carries `simulation_id` and `model`, so you
can go from the file to model_describe_simulation without guessing.

A 'data' entry that is already cached on this server also carries
`variables`, each with its name, units and long_name, so you can pick the
file that holds what was asked for without opening them one by one. An
entry that is not cached yet carries `variables_note` instead, which says
to call model_list_variables on it, and an entry that could not be read
carries `variables_error`. Judge a file by its variables, not by its
filename: a file named for an external model can still hold the variable
the question needs.

Each 'data' entry also carries `origin`. `surimi-run` is output a SURIMI run
wrote. `external-or-reference` is data served for comparison and is NOT a
SURIMI result: an answer built on it must name the file it came from and
must not present it as what SURIMI found. `surimi-sample` is real SURIMI
output bundled with this server rather than held in S3 -- currently just
the western-Med sample -- readable through this server exactly like any
other 'data' entry.

The default listing (no `prefix`) also carries every file bundled under
this server's own data/netcdf-samples/ directory, regardless of what the
S3 prefix scan finds. When SURIMI_LOCAL_NETCDF_SAMPLES additionally names
an operator-supplied local directory, its .nc files are merged in too --
origin `external-or-reference`, not `surimi-sample`: unlike the bundled
directory, a file's presence there is not verified to be the genuine
sample just because it shares a name with one.
name: model_list_files

description:
List the named regions in a mask file so you can pick a region by name.

Returns {mask_file, n_regions, regions:[{name, n_cells}]}. Call this BEFORE
model_time_series or model_trend (which take a region NAME), and to know
which regions model_top_regions will rank. Do NOT guess region names or call
model_top_regions on the mask itself to discover them.
name: model_list_regions

description:
List SURIMI simulation runs found in object storage, newest first.

Call this FIRST for any question about a model RUN or experiment. Returns
{count, simulations:[{model, simulation_id, n_artifacts, last_modified,
kinds, summary, stock}], scanned, as_of, stale, note, partial,
partial_note, denied_run_like_keys, denied_note, summaries_omitted,
summaries_omitted_note, summaries_failed, summaries_failed_note}.
`scanned` lists which models actually have at least one run right now -
that is what answers "which models have runs". `model` filters to one
model (e.g. 'surimi-cmsy'). Then call model_describe_simulation on a
simulation_id to see full artifact/metadata detail for just that run.

`summary` is a short, human-readable line built from the run's own
parsed metadata - for CMSY, the STOCK plus year range and biomass type
(e.g. "Hogfish - Florida Keys, 1986-2012, CPUE"); for market, its
config-file coverage. Read `summary` (and `stock`) here to answer "what
is run X about" / "which stock did it assess" WITHOUT calling
model_describe_simulation on every run in the list - that is the whole
point of this field. `summary` is null when the model has no parser,
the parser found nothing to say, or the parse was refused (a truncated
or ambiguous id_file.csv) - null always means unknown, never a
placeholder or a guess; do not infer a stock from a filename yourself.
`stock` sits alongside `summary` only for runs where a stock was
actually determined (CMSY today) - read `stock`, not `summary`, when
asked specifically "which stock". A run beyond the newest ones
summarised in this call does not carry a `summary` key AT ALL - that is
different from `summary: null` ("attempted, nothing to report") - the
top-level `summaries_omitted` count says how many were skipped to bound
cost this call, and `summaries_omitted_note` explains; call
model_describe_simulation directly on any of those by simulation_id.

`summaries_failed` counts runs (within this call's summarised set)
whose summary could NOT be computed this call because of a storage
error while fetching - a property of the moment (a network blip, an
expiring STS token), not a fact about the run - rather than a
deliberate parser refusal. Those runs show `summary: null` exactly like
a genuine refusal, but are retried on the next call rather than staying
null forever - do not treat their null as a final answer the way a real
refusal's null is; say the summary was unavailable this call rather
than that the run has none. `summaries_failed_note` explains when it is
above zero.

A COLD call (nothing cached yet) fetches summaries for up to
_SUMMARY_CAP runs concurrently, which can still take a few seconds even
though it is no longer one round trip per run done in series - mention
that a first call may be slower than a later one rather than assuming
every call is instant.

stale=true means object storage was unreachable and this is the
last good listing - say so rather than presenting it as current.
partial=true means some objects could not be listed even in a fresh
scan, so counts here (n_artifacts, kinds) may be short - say that too,
do not present them as exact. denied_run_like_keys is a COVERAGE hint,
not a degradation - this listing itself is correct and current - it
counts objects that look like simulation runs but sit under a
deliberately-excluded area of storage (housekeeping/lake prefixes, e.g.
"raw/", "processed/") and so are never scanned for runs at all. When it
is above zero, mention that some run-like objects exist outside the
scanned area (see denied_note) rather than implying this listing is the
entire ensemble's coverage.
name: model_list_simulations

description:
List data variables in a netcdf file with shapes, dtypes, units.

`file` is accepted as an alias for `path`.
name: model_list_variables

description:
Resolve a reference-vocabulary code to its meaning. Read this FIRST for
"what species is ANK" / "what does gear code X mean" / "what country is
ESP" - never guess a code's meaning from memory, this tool is the source
of truth for what the FAO/ISSCFG/ISO standards actually say.

`kind` is one of "species" (FAO 3-alpha, cross-referenced to WoRMS
taxonomy and FishBase common name when they join), "gear" (ISSCFG
fishery/gear code), or "country" (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3) - or omitted to
search all three. Omitting `kind` does NOT guess a domain from the
code's shape; it checks all three vocabularies and reports every REAL
hit. This matters because the vocabularies genuinely collide: FAO
species codes and ISO country codes share the same 3-letter alphabet, so
e.g. "ESP" is both Spain (ISO 3166) and Setipinna phasa / Gangetic
hairfin anchovy (FAO/ASFIS) - a real collision, not a bug. When more than
one domain matches, `ambiguous: true` and `matches` lists all of them;
read `ambiguity_note` and do not present either as THE answer without
picking a domain via `kind`. When exactly one domain matches (the common
case), its fields are merged directly into the top-level result.

An unknown code returns `found: false` with `suggestions` - real entries
from the searched vocabulary/vocabularies that are textually close, from
difflib against the actual code list, never an invented name. An empty
`suggestions` list means nothing close was found either; still not a
guess.

`degraded` (only present when non-empty) lists which underlying source(s)
could not be loaded this call - a network blip or expiring STS token,
not proof the code does not exist; a real answer from an unaffected
source can still appear alongside a `degraded` entry for one that
failed.

These are external standards (FAO/ISSCAAP, ISSCFG, WoRMS, FishBase, ISO
3166) the SURIMI project consumes for coding its own data - not SURIMI
output.
name: model_lookup_code

description:
B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy per stock from a run's NetCDF (stock_status,
exploitation on year x species), with each stock's Kobe position.

Use this for the status of WESTERN MEDITERRANEAN stocks in SURIMI's
runs: whether a stock is overfished, has improved or deteriorated, or is
recovering. It reads the first NetCDF file of the run. Without `stock` it
returns every stock's position in `year` (default: the last year) and the
count per Kobe quadrant, which answers "the stock" when no stock was
named. With `stock` (a code such as "HKE", or a label such as "HKE
adult") it returns that stock's position in `year` (default: its latest
year), its first assessed year and its full trajectory.

Returns {simulation_id, source_file, semantics_note, year, n_stocks,
counts, stocks} or {simulation_id, source_file, semantics_note, stock,
first_assessed_year, latest: {year, b_bmsy, f_fmsy, kobe}, trajectory},
plus stale/note/partial/partial_note; or {error, ...}. Read
semantics_note before reporting: there are no uncertainty bounds, and
historical and simulated years are not distinguished.
name: model_run_stock_status

description:
Reverse lookup: a species name or fragment to codes, searched
case-insensitively across ASFIS (scientific + English name), WoRMS
(scientific name), and FishBase (common name + binomial). Use this when
you have a name, not a code - e.g. "what's the FAO code for anchovy".

Each result carries `source` ("asfis" | "worms" | "fishbase") so a
caller can tell an FAO alpha-3 code apart from a FishBase common-name
hit rather than assuming every result is the same kind of thing.

All three sources are searched in full and results are RANKED BY MATCH
QUALITY, then capped at `limit` total (not `limit` per source). A name
that contains the query as a word ("Red hake" for "hake") always outranks
one that merely contains it inside a longer word ("Capoetobrama
kuschakewitschi"); an exact whole-name match outranks both. Equal matches
are ordered by whether FAO keeps capture statistics for the species, then
source, then alphabetically.

`total_matches` appears when the cap hid results. Treat a large value as
"the query is ambiguous, not answered": 21 ASFIS species are named
"... hake", so ranking cannot know which one is meant - narrow the query
(a binomial, or the full common name) rather than reporting the first hit
as THE answer.

`degraded` (only present when non-empty) names any source that could not
be searched this call; results from unaffected sources still come back.
name: model_search_taxon

description:
Time series of `var` within one region, returned as a compact cube slice.

Returns a `summary` (n_points, n_valid, value_start/end/min/max/mean,
slope_per_step, direction) and `by_year` (one pivotable row per calendar
year: {year, value, n_steps}) plus provenance. Present the summary and the
by_year rows (a small table or chart); cite the single calculation record
(receipt) for the whole block. By default the raw per-step series is NOT returned -- a global file
has hundreds of monthly steps and enumerating them floods the reply. For
"is it increasing/decreasing" or "what is the trend" use model_trend (it
adds a significance test and reads the full series internally).

`points_for_years` is [first_year, last_year], both inclusive, and adds
`points` (one {t, value, year} per timestep in that window) plus
`points_window`. Ask for it ONLY when the question needs resolution finer
than a year -- a seasonal cycle, which month a peak fell in, a spike inside
one year -- because by_year has already averaged that away. Keep the window
to the years actually asked about: a window over 120 timesteps is refused,
not trimmed. The summary and by_year still cover the WHOLE series, so do
not read a windowed `points` as the full record.

`select` picks one coordinate on an extra dimension, e.g.
{"species": "herring"}. A value found at several positions is refused,
and the error names the positions, so pass the position number instead.
Omitted on a variable that has such a dimension, the value AVERAGES
across it and the reply names the dimension in `unselected_dims`.
name: model_time_series

description:
Top N regions by aggregated value of `var`, optionally within one year.

When `year` is given, only that calendar year's timesteps are loaded
(lazy .isel before .values), so global multi-decade files do not blow
memory. When `year` is omitted on a file that spans MULTIPLE years, the
most recent year THAT ACTUALLY HAS DATA is used automatically (reported in
provenance.year with year_defaulted=true + a coverage note) -- aggregating
every year of a global file is slow enough to time out. Pass an explicit
year to cover a different period; an explicit year is always honoured as
given, even if it is empty. Returns a rank-ordered list with values,
provenance, and coverage.

`agg` defaults to "mean": it previously had no default, so the natural
tool call omitted it and died on argument validation before reaching data.

`select` is {dimension: coordinate_value} for any extra non-time,
non-spatial axis the variable carries (species, functional group, fleet).
Without it a catch variable shaped (time, species, lat, lon) is averaged
across cod and herring into one number belonging to neither, so when such a
dimension is left unselected the result carries coverage.unselected_dims
and a note listing the dimension and its values.
name: model_top_regions

description:
Estimate a monotonic trend with Mann-Kendall + linear slope.

PREFERRED for "is X increasing/decreasing", "what is the trend", or "how has
X changed over time" questions. Returns a compact result: slope (linear
regression on time index), Mann-Kendall p_value, a categorical direction
(increasing/decreasing/no_trend), n (valid points), and n_missing (NaN gaps
skipped). Answer directly from these fields.
name: model_trend

description:
Check that a region mask sits on the same lat/lon grid as the data file.

Returns {aligned: bool, mismatches: [...]} naming each axis that differs
('lat'/'lon' for a differing axis, 'lat_missing'/'lon_missing' when a file
carries no such coordinate). An axis matches when its shape is equal and its
values agree within 1e-3. model_top_regions, model_time_series,
model_compare_periods and model_trend apply the mask cell by cell without
re-projecting it, so each runs this check first and refuses a mask on a
different grid. Call this to see which axis differs, and whenever a data
file and a mask come from different sources. If aligned is False, report
the mismatch and give no regional numbers for that pair.
name: model_validate_alignment

description:
Verify a signed calculation record (the `receipt`) against the server's signing key.

Returns {verified, reason, verification_method, recompute_supported,
recompute_note}. `verification_method` is always "signature_only" here:
this server has no recompute path for any tool, so a passing check means
the record is unaltered since issue, NOT that the number was recomputed.
That is a weaker claim and the two must not be confused.

A signature mismatch returns verified false and does not raise, and so does
a server with no signing key (reason "secret_not_configured"). Records
issued before the model/data rename carry legacy nc_* tool_ids; those still
verify unchanged, because the signature covers the stored payload, not the
current tool name.
name: model_verify
